'''Armed conflicts and attacks'''
*[[Russian invasion of Ukraine]]
**The [[Russian Navy]] patrol ship ''[[Russian patrol ship Sergey Kotov|Sergey Kotov]]'' is sunk in the [[Black Sea]] after being struck by [[Ukraine|Ukrainian]] [[MAGURA V5]] [[Unmanned surface vehicle|naval drones]]. [https://www.theguardian.com/world/2024/mar/05/ukraine-russian-warship-occupied-crimea-sinking (''The Guardian'')]
*[[Territorial disputes in the South China Sea]]
**Four [[Philippine Coast Guard]] sailors are injured in [[Territorial disputes in the South China Sea|contested water]]s when [[watercannon]]s are deployed by the [[Chinese Coast Guard]]. The vessels were escorting a resupply convoy to a [[BRP Sierra Madre#Philippine Navy|Philippine outpost]] in [[disputed territory]] at [[Second Thomas Shoal]] in the [[South China Sea]], claimed by several nations. [https://www.cnn.com/2024/03/06/asia/philippines-china-south-china-sea-confrontation-intl-hnk-dst/index.html (CNN)]
** The ''Tesla Volcano Group Shutdown'' (Vulkangruppe Tesla Abschalten) claimed an arson attack on a power pylon near Tesla's car factory outside Berlin. The fire caused production halt that is expected on various days.[https://www.dw.com/en/arson-near-teslas-gigafactory-who-is-the-volcano-group/a-68457754 (Deutsche Welle)]

**Three civilians killed in an Israeli airstrike on [[Hula, Lebanon|Hula]].[https://arab.news/y2xsh (Arab News)]

*[[Russian invasion of Ukraine]]
**[[International Criminal Court investigation in Ukraine]]
***The [[International Criminal Court]] issues [[arrest warrants]] for [[Sergey Kobylash]], the commander of the [[Russian Long Range Aviation|Long-Range Aviation]] of the [[Russian Aerospace Forces]], and [[Viktor Sokolov (naval officer)|Viktor Sokolov]], the commander of the [[Black Sea Fleet]], for their involvement in [[Russian strikes against Ukrainian infrastructure (2022–present)|Russian strikes against Ukrainian infrastructure]]. Kwon was arrested in March 2023 in Montenegro. [https://apnews.com/article/montenegro-do-kwon-terraform-labs-extradition-overturned-37a2a6934b144e27348d8b3c78f2c971 (AP)]

***The [[Republican Party (United States)|Republican Party]] holds [[2024 Republican Party presidential primaries|presidential nominating contests]] in [[2024 Alabama Republican presidential primary|Alabama]], [[2024 Alaska Republican presidential primary|Alaska]], [[2024 Arkansas Republican presidential primary|Arkansas]], [[2024 California Republican presidential primary|California]], [[2024 Colorado Republican presidential primary|Colorado]], [[2024 Maine Republican presidential primary|Maine]], [[2024 Massachusetts Republican presidential primary|Massachusetts]], [[2024 Minnesota Republican presidential primary|Minnesota]], [[2024 North Carolina Republican presidential primary|North Carolina]], [[2024 Oklahoma Republican presidential primary|Oklahoma]], [[2024 Tennessee Republican presidential primary|Tennessee]], [[2024 Texas Republican presidential primary|Texas]], [[2024 Utah Republican presidential caucuses|Utah]], [[2024 Vermont Republican presidential primary|Vermont]], and [[2024 Virginia Republican presidential primary|Virginia]]. ***[[President of the United States|U.S. President]] [[Joe Biden]] and former president [[Donald Trump]] win their respective contests on Super Tuesday with one-third of the delegates. Former [[United States Ambassador to the United Nations|U.S. Ambassador]] [[Nikki Haley]] wins the [[Vermont]] primary, securing her first statewide victory in the Republican parties. [[Jason Palmer (politician)|Jason Palmer]] wins the [[2024 American Samoa presidential caucuses|American Samoa]] Democratic Presidential caucus. [https://www.washingtonpost.com/elections/2024/03/05/super-tuesday-live-updates-election-2024/ (''The Washington Post'')]
